title: Context Parallelism for Scalable Million-Token Inference
problem: Long-context LLM inference (prefill of sequences up to 1M tokens) exceeds single-GPU memory and compute capacity, requiring efficient distributed strategies across many GPUs.
motivation: State-of-the-art LLMs serving very long contexts (documents, code, multi-modal) need near-linear scaling of prefill latency with GPU count. Existing KV-cache replication across GPUs wastes memory and existing ring-attention implementations have load imbalance under causal masking.
method: Context Parallelism (CP) partitions the input sequence across GPUs along the sequence dimension. Two ring-attention variants are developed: pass-KV (circulates Key/Value tensors across a GPU ring, each GPU holds fixed Q blocks) and pass-Q (circulates Query tensors, each GPU holds fixed KV). Load-balanced sharding uses 2N chunks per sequence to balance causal attention across N GPUs. Adaptive selection switches between pass-KV and pass-Q based on KV-cache miss rate to cover full prefill, persistent KV prefill, and decode phases.
key_novelty: Two complementary ring-attention algorithms (pass-KV and pass-Q) with load-balanced 2N-chunk sharding that eliminates causal-mask imbalance, plus adaptive mode selection covering all inference phases. Demonstrated on commodity RDMA and TCP interconnects showing bandwidth-tolerance.
contributions: Pass-KV ring attention: each GPU holds query chunks and receives rotating KV blocks for full causal attention without redundancy
Pass-Q ring attention: each GPU holds KV cache and receives rotating query blocks, optimal for persistent KV prefill and decode
Load-balanced 2N chunk partitioning to equalize work under causal masking
Adaptive pass-KV vs pass-Q selection based on KV-cache miss threshold
Scaling to 1M context prefill in 77s on 128 H100 GPUs (93% parallelization efficiency, 63% FLOPS utilization)
Benchmarks on both RDMA and TCP showing similar scalability, validating medium-to-low bandwidth commercial datacenter deployments
baselines: Existing ring attention without load balancing
limitations: Efficiency drops somewhat at very high GPU counts due to communication overhead; requires custom attention kernels; 63% FLOPS utilization leaves headroom; TCP interconnect slightly worse than RDMA in absolute latency.
